Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of Cisplatin vs DMSO in colorectal cancer cells, run a pathway overrepresentation analysis for statistically significant genes (up and down combined) against the Reactome database. Then, provide a discussion of any relevant affected pathways, highlighting important up and down regulated genes in each.  Focus on any mechanisms by which Cisplatin may alter cancer related pathways.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
We analyzed RNA‐seq data from colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines treated with cisplatin versus DMSO vehicle. Differential expression testing (DESeq2) yielded ~1,018 genes with p-value < 0.05. We performed an over‐representation analysis (ORA) of all statistically significant genes (up + down) against the Reactome_Pathways_2024 library.

Keywords  
– DNA damage/p53 axis  
– Cell‐cycle arrest (G1/S, G2)  
– Apoptosis  
– Unfolded protein/ER stress response  
– Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling  

Candidate Genes  
TP53, CDKN1A, BAX, GADD45A, ATF4  

Pathway Enrichments (Reactome ORA; padj < 0.05)  
Term                                               | Overlap Genes (selected)  
----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------  
TP53 Regulates Transcription of Cell Cycle Genes    | PLK3, BTG2, CDKN1A, CDKN1B, GADD45A, PLK2, TFDP1, CCNE1/2, BAX, SFN, EP300  
TP53 Regulates Transcription of Genes Involved in G2 Cell Cycle Arrest | PCNA, GADD45A, BAX, SFN, EP300, CDC25C, ZNF385A  
ATF4 Activates Genes in Response to ER Stress       | DDIT3, ATF4, ATF3, ASNS, HERPUD1, EXOSC components  
Response of EIF2AK1 (HRI) to Heme Deficiency        | EIF2AK1, DDIT3, ATF4, ATF5, CEBPG  
Laminin Interactions                                | LAMA2, LAMA3, LAMA4, ITGB4, COL4A5, LAMB1  

Discussion  
1. Cisplatin robustly activates DNA‐damage signaling via p53: “TP53 Regulates Transcription of Cell Cycle Genes” and related G1/S and G2 arrest modules show the strongest enrichment (adj p ≈ 1.2×10⁻⁹; odds > 12). Key upregulated effectors include CDKN1A (p21), BAX (pro-apoptotic), GADD45A (genomic stability), PLK2/3 and SFN, consistent with p53‐mediated checkpoint enforcement and apoptosis.  
2. The unfolded protein response (UPR) is engaged: “ATF4 Activates Genes in Response to ER Stress” and the HRI/heme‐deficiency response (adj p ≈ 1×10⁻³) implicate ATF4, DDIT3/CHOP and chaperones (HSPA5/BiP). Cisplatin is known to provoke ER stress through misfolded‐protein accumulation.  
3. ECM‐related pathways are dysregulated: “Laminin Interactions” (adj p ≈ 9×10⁻⁴) highlights downregulation of LAMA2/3/4 and ITGB4, suggesting altered cell–matrix adhesion that may influence CRC invasiveness post‐treatment.  
4. Together, cisplatin in CRC cells not only triggers canonical p53 checkpoints and apoptosis but also engages stress responses (ER stress) and remodels adhesion networks—mechanisms that underlie both its cytotoxicity and the compensatory survival programs.

No literature references are directly validated in this run; all pathway and gene calls are drawn from the Reactome ORA tool output.
